title: Headaches and hydration
content: Mild dehydration is a well-known trigger for tension-type headaches. Fluid loss across a day, especially in warm weather, can bring on head pain that eases after rehydrating over a few hours.

title: Sleep debt and daytime symptoms
content: Consistently sleeping less than the recommended seven to nine hours builds a cumulative sleep debt, commonly linked with daytime fatigue, poor concentration, irritability and headaches.

title: Skipped meals and low energy
content: Going long stretches without eating can cause blood sugar to dip, which many people experience as tiredness, shakiness, difficulty concentrating or a dull headache in the afternoon.

title: Daily water intake
content: General guidance suggests most adults need roughly two litres of fluid a day, though needs vary with body size, activity level and climate. Thirst and pale-coloured urine are practical everyday indicators.

title: When to see a doctor about a headache
content: Seek medical attention if a headache is sudden and severe, follows a head injury, comes with fever, a stiff neck, confusion, vision changes or weakness, or if headaches are becoming more frequent over time.

title: Fatigue and its common causes
content: Ongoing tiredness most often traces back to everyday factors such as inadequate sleep, dehydration, irregular eating, low physical activity or stress. Persistent fatigue that does not improve with rest is worth discussing with a clinician.
